extra.message: POST /ops/bundle/loan-thaw-178 passes attacker-controlled request bytes, optionally base64-decoded, directly to pickle.loads(). A caller possessing the configured INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN can execute arbitrary Python code with the server's privileges.

POST /ops/dock/loan-shelf-594 joins the user-controlled name parameter to BASE_EXPORT_DIR without containment validation and writes the request body there. A caller possessing INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN can use ../ components or an absolute path to create or overwrite arbitrary files writable by the server.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory

extra.message: POST /ops/xml/loan-fold-614 parses the request body with load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, and no_network=False. When lxml is installed, a caller possessing INTERNAL_OPS_TOKEN can cause the parser to resolve attacker-selected external entities, including local file references and network resources supported by its libxml2 build. The handler returns only the root tag, so direct disclosure of entity contents is not established.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: POST /ops/wire/loan-underwrite-roll-068 logs the complete underwriting request body and Authorization header at warning level without redaction. Requests passing the internal-token gate can therefore expose submitted financial information and bearer credentials to log readers.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: When SECRET_KEY is unset, live session signing and verification use the publicly known constant dev-only-change-me-for-local-runs. An attacker can forge an HS256 loan_session token containing an active administrator's user ID and authenticate as that administrator.

cwe: CWE-321: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key

extra.message: The admin Invite workflow initializes every new account with DemoPass123!, submits that password to /api/admin/users at line 989, and provides no password input. The backend creates an immediately active account with the supplied password, including for the selectable admin role. Anyone knowing a newly created account's email can log in using this publicly displayed password until it is changed.

API-key authentication checks only the key's active flag and hash, ignoring the owner's is_active flag and current role. Disabling or demoting an administrator does not revoke their keys. Those keys retain access to arbitrary application statuses, business names, and decision details through /api/integrations/applications/{application_id}/status.

Session validation checks the JWT and account activity without checking revocation or password-change state. Logout only deletes the browser cookie, while password changes and resets only update the password hash. A copied session token remains usable after these actions until its original expiration, normally 12 hours.

COOKIE_SECURE defaults to false, causing the authentication cookie to be issued without Secure. With this configuration, browsers can transmit the session token over an HTTP connection to the application host, exposing it to network interception.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: The public login endpoint verifies passwords without an attempt counter, delay, lockout, or application-level rate limiter. Failed attempts immediately return and leave no throttling state, allowing repeated password guessing and credential stuffing against known accounts.

cwe: CWE-307: Improper Restriction of Excessive Authentication Attempts

extra.message: Unauthenticated registration returns HTTP 409 with 'Email is already registered' specifically when the submitted email exists. An attacker supplying otherwise valid registration fields can distinguish registered accounts from unused addresses.

GET /api/borrowers/{borrower_id} permits an underwriter to read a profile whenever it has any unassigned application, without the ACTIVE_QUEUE_STATUSES restriction enforced by can_view_application(). An underwriter can enumerate borrower IDs and obtain tax-ID suffixes, contact details, addresses, and revenue for borrowers whose only applications are private unsubmitted drafts.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: The document review queue includes all unassigned applications for underwriters, omitting the active-queue status restriction used by application authorization. Consequently, uploaded documents belonging to unsubmitted drafts appear in /api/documents/review-queue, exposing business names, filenames, document categories, and review metadata even when the corresponding application detail is forbidden.

Requesting a document unconditionally changes an application's status to needs_documents, including approved, rejected, and withdrawn applications. Support specialists can invoke this route for any application despite lacking decision privileges. This overwrites the final status and re-enables borrower editing and submission through routes that accept needs_documents.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: Application updates check only whether the selected product is active before saving the requested amount and term. Unlike creation at lines 845-848, updates do not enforce the product's amount range or offered terms. A borrower can create a valid draft, PATCH it with values outside those product limits, and submit it because submission does not repeat these checks.

cwe: CWE-1284: Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input

extra.message: The required-document gate used when recording decisions checks only status == 'accepted', ignoring expires_at. An accepted KYC document remains eligible after its actual expiration until the separate reminder script updates its status. During that interval, a final loan decision can be recorded using expired required documentation.

cwe: CWE-841: Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow

extra.message: Document acceptance checks only the previously loaded status, without locking the row or checking a document version or content hash. The upload route concurrently permits replacement of an uploaded document. A borrower can replace its bytes while an underwriter's acceptance is in progress, leaving the replacement accepted even though the underwriter reviewed the previous file.

Every document replacement writes a new UUID-named file and replaces stored_filename without deleting the previous file. Because uploaded documents can be replaced repeatedly and there is no cumulative storage quota, a self-registered borrower can repeatedly upload files within the per-file limit to one document and exhaust server disk space with orphaned uploads.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: csv_response writes cells without neutralizing spreadsheet formula prefixes. Borrowers control business_name, which appears in application, decision, and document exports; underwriters also control exported decision text. Values beginning with '=' can therefore become executable spreadsheet formulas when an administrator opens an exported CSV, enabling malicious links or data exfiltration depending on the spreadsheet application.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File
